correct_completion: have I seen such a beautiful sunset.
full_sentence: Never in my life have I seen such a beautiful sunset.
acceptable_variants: have I witnessed such a stunning landscape.
have I felt so moved by a view.

options.text: I have seen such a beautiful sunset.
options.why_wrong: After a fronted negative phrase such as 'never', the auxiliary must come before the subject. The normal word order here is incorrect.

options.text: have I seen such a beautiful sunset.
I have never seen such a beautiful sunset.
options.why_wrong: 'Never' is already fronted in the stem, so repeating it in the normal position is redundant and breaks the emphatic structure.

options.text: I had seen such a beautiful sunset.
options.why_wrong: The past perfect does not fit a experience that extends up to the present. The present perfect with inversion is needed.

explanation: When a negative phrase such as 'never' is moved to the front of a sentence for emphasis, English requires subject-auxiliary inversion. Portuguese speakers often keep the normal subject-verb order after a fronted negative, because Portuguese word order is more flexible and does not require inversion in this structure.
translation: Em toda a minha vida, nunca vi um pôr do sol tão bonito.
